lesson.subject: data-ai
lesson.title: Pattern Spotters
lesson.summary: Find patterns in pictures and sounds the way a machine does to sort things.
learning_objectives: Find a pattern in a set of examples
Say how a machine uses patterns to sort
Know a pattern guess can be wrong

standards.text: Learning: computers can learn from data
Identify and describe patterns in data visualisations

success_criteria: I can say what comes next in a pattern
I can sort things with a rule
I know a machine's guess can be wrong
lesson.real_life: Rangoli and truck art, tiled floors and the days of the week.

blocks.markdown: Today's big question: how do machines find patterns?
blocks.say: Today we look for patterns. Aisha wants to teach her robot friend to spot them.

blocks.alt: A floor of black, white and grey square tiles in a repeating pattern
blocks.caption: A tiled floor with a repeating pattern.
blocks.credit: Photo by note thanun on Unsplash
blocks.say: Look at this floor. The same shapes come again and again. That is a pattern.

blocks.text: Stop 1: Patterns in shapes and sounds

blocks.markdown: A **pattern** repeats in a set way.
blocks.say: A pattern is something that repeats in a set way. Colours, shapes and sounds can make patterns.

scenes.caption: Colour pattern.
scenes.say: Red, blue, red, blue. The colours take turns. It is a pattern.

scenes.caption: Sound pattern.
scenes.say: Clap, stamp, clap, stamp. Sounds can make a pattern too.

scenes.caption: What is next?
scenes.say: After a pattern, we can say what comes next.

question.prompt: Red, blue, red, blue, ... What comes next?
question.explanation: The pattern goes red then blue, so red is next.

blocks.markdown: Days of the week repeat in a **cycle**.
blocks.say: Days make a pattern. Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday, and then Monday again after Sunday.

scenes.caption: A week.
scenes.say: Seven days make one week. They go in the same order.

scenes.caption: Again.
scenes.say: After Sunday, a new week starts with Monday.

scenes.caption: A cycle.
scenes.say: A pattern that repeats is a cycle.

question.prompt: The days of the week form a repeating pattern.

blocks.title: Aisha's scarf robot
blocks.transcript: Aisha has a robot friend. She wants to teach it patterns. She shows a striped scarf. She says the label: striped. Then a spotty scarf. She says: spotty. She only shows two. The robot gets confused. So she shows many more. Each one has a label. Now a new scarf. The robot looks for the pattern. The robot guesses: striped. It is right! But a robot can still be wrong. People check its guesses.
blocks.caption: Aisha shows her robot friend striped and spotty scarves.

points: A pattern repeats in a set way
Patterns can be seen and heard
A repeating pattern is a cycle
blocks.say: Let us remember. Patterns repeat. They can be colours, shapes, sounds or days.

terms.meaning: Something that repeats in a set way.
A pattern that goes round and round.
What comes after.
To happen again.
How something looks, like red or blue.

mini_quiz.hint: Think about red, blue, red, blue.

options.text: Something that repeats in a set way

mini_quiz.prompt: A sound can make a pattern.
Which day comes after Sunday in a new week?

blocks.markdown: To **sort** is to put things that are alike into groups.
blocks.say: A machine can sort things into groups. It looks at things that are alike.

scenes.caption: Many cups.
scenes.say: Here are cups in many colours. Aisha will sort them.

scenes.caption: Two groups.
scenes.say: Red cups go in one box. Blue cups go in another.

scenes.caption: Sorted.
scenes.say: Sorting by colour is one way to sort.

question.prompt: Aisha sorts cups by colour. How many groups for red and blue cups?
question.explanation: Red cups are one group. Blue cups are another.

blocks.say: A rule says how to sort. Rule: put animals with four legs in one box.

scenes.caption: The rule.
scenes.say: The rule: four legs go in the first box. Others go in the second.

scenes.caption: Apply the rule.
scenes.say: A cat has four legs. A bird has two legs.

scenes.caption: Sorted by the rule.
scenes.say: The cat goes in box one. The bird goes in box two.

blocks.title: Sort at home
instructions: Choose one rule, such as colour or size.
Sort everything into groups using your rule.
Try a different rule. Do the groups change?
blocks.say: Now you try. Sort things at home with a grown-up.

question.prompt: The same things can be sorted in different ways.

points: A rule says how to sort
blocks.say: Let us remember. Sorting puts alike things together. A rule says how.

terms.meaning: To put things that are alike into groups.
A sentence that says how to do something.
Things that belong together.
Parts an animal walks on.
A container to hold a group.

mini_quiz.prompt: What does a rule do when sorting?
mini_quiz.hint: It tells you what to do.
mini_quiz.explanation: A rule says how to sort.

mini_quiz.prompt: There is only one way to sort a pile of toys.
mini_quiz.explanation: There are many ways to sort.

mini_quiz.prompt: A bird has two legs. Which box for the rule 'four legs'?
mini_quiz.explanation: Two legs does not fit four legs.

blocks.markdown: A pattern helps us **predict** the next one.
blocks.say: Spotting a pattern lets us guess what comes next. A machine does this too.

scenes.caption: Look.
scenes.say: Spot, stripe, spot, stripe. What is next?

scenes.caption: Predict.
scenes.say: The pattern is spot, stripe. So the next one is a spot.

scenes.caption: Check.
scenes.say: The guess can be wrong. We check the next one.

question.prompt: Spot, stripe, spot, stripe. What is next?
question.explanation: After a stripe comes a spot.

blocks.markdown: Play the memory game. Then find the **odd one out**.
blocks.say: First a memory game. Then find the odd one out.

question.explanation: Blue is different from the two reds.

points: Spot a pattern to guess what comes next
The odd one out is different
blocks.say: Let us remember. A pattern helps us guess. A guess can be wrong.

terms.meaning: To say what will come next.
The one that is different from the others.
To say what you think without being sure.
To make sure.
A long line of colour.

mini_quiz.prompt: Red, red, blue, red, red, blue. What is next?
mini_quiz.explanation: The pattern is red, red, blue.

mini_quiz.prompt: A guess from a pattern can sometimes be wrong.
mini_quiz.explanation: A guess is not always right.

mini_quiz.prompt: What is the odd one out?
mini_quiz.explanation: The odd one out is different from the rest.

blocks.markdown: An **example** shows what something is like.
blocks.say: Aisha wants her robot friend to tell striped scarves from spotty ones. She shows examples.

blocks.alt: A close-up of woven fabric in orange, blue, red and turquoise threads
blocks.caption: A woven cloth. Aisha shows her robot different patterns.
blocks.credit: Photo by Mikaela Wiedenhoff on Unsplash
blocks.say: This cloth has a woven pattern. Aisha shows the robot many scarves with different patterns.
She shows a striped scarf and says, striped. She shows a spotty scarf and says, spotty.

blocks.title: Teach a friend
instructions: Show five striped things. Say: striped.
Show five spotty things. Say: spotty.
Show a new thing. Can your friend guess?
blocks.say: More examples help the robot learn. One example is not enough.

question.prompt: Why does Aisha show many examples?
question.explanation: Many examples help a machine learn.

options.text: To help the robot learn the pattern

blocks.text: Stop 2: Test with a new one

blocks.markdown: **Test** with a new example the robot has not seen.
blocks.say: Now Aisha shows a new scarf. The robot guesses. It says, striped. It is right.

scenes.caption: A new scarf.
scenes.say: A new scarf with thin stripes comes in.

scenes.caption: Good guess.
scenes.say: The robot guesses: striped. Aisha says, correct!

scenes.caption: A mistake.
scenes.say: A scarf with spots and a few stripes confuses it. It guesses wrong.

question.prompt: The robot guesses wrong. What can Aisha do?

options.text: Show more examples and try again

blocks.say: Let us remember. Show many examples with labels. Test with new ones.

terms.meaning: One case that shows what something is like.

A machine that follows instructions.
To help someone or something learn.
